stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy criticises Trump for calling Putin his ‘friend’; Kyiv deploys new laser weapon
stories.summary: Ukrainian leader likens Putin to Hitler; laser system intercepts Russian drone but not ready for ‘mass deployment’. What we know on day 1,739 Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticised Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin his “friend” , likening the Russian leader to Adolf Hitler . “Of course it’s up to the president of the United States, but ... it’s strange,” the Ukrainian leader told the BBC in an interview aired on Friday. “He is an aggressor, and a killer... He can’t be a friend. Just cannot be. It’s the same that somebody says about Hitler during the second world war, that he’s a good friend. No. He’s not a friend.” Zelenskyy said what was needed was “more progress” and urged Washington to increase pressure on Moscow. Ukraine has for the first time used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered drone , according to its state-backed defence group Brave1. An adviser to Zelenskyy, Serhiy Beskrestnov, published footage earlier this week showing a target crashing in a fireball, saying a Russian Geran jet drone had been shot down by a laser system for the “first time”. Agence France-Presse quoted Brave1 as saying on Friday: “Footage recently emerged online showing a Ukrainian laser system being used in combat to intercept an enemy jet-powered drone.” The weapon was developed by a recipient of a Brave1 grant and operated by a private air defence team, Brave1 added. But it cautioned that “a first successful interception does not mean the technology is ready for mass deployment”. “Laser air defence remains an experimental technology,” it said, adding that at least seven teams in Ukraine were currently working on laser weapons. Beskrestnov said the system, known as Blysk and developed by the Ukrainian company Carmine Sky, was protecting critical infrastructure during the interception. A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles bound for Libya has turned around in the Mediterranean after Ukrainian maritime drones sank ⁠a Russian naval warship in Benghazi ⁠port last Sunday, Reuters quoted ​three people from military and security services as saying on Friday. The convoy, which was escorted by the Russian navy frigate Golovko, turned around near the strait of Sicily on the same day as ⁠the attack in Benghazi, said a European military official who had been tracking the convoy. A Ukrainian military intelligence official and a Middle East security official confirmed the flotilla had turned from heading to Libya. Russia’s defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Ukraine has offered ⁠a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food ⁠exports and ⁠passed this ​on to international allies , the foreign minister ⁠said. “We are ready for ⁠a ceasefire. We are ​grateful to ‌India, Turkey and ‌Egypt, which are playing ‌an active and important role in de-escalating tensions in the Black Sea, as well as in mediation efforts. ‌We are now awaiting a response from ​Russia,” Andrii Sybiha was cited by public broadcaster Suspilne as saying on Friday. He added that Russia had proposed ⁠Ukraine suspend attacks on the ​Russian ​oil sector under ​the truce, but ​Kyiv ‌would only consider ​this ​as part of a bigger energy ceasefire deal. Ukraine’s military said on ⁠Friday it ⁠had struck ​a Russian solid ⁠rocket fuel production site ⁠in ​the Tula ‌region south ‌of Moscow ‌overnight. “The plant is the starting point of the ‌missile production chain: it manufactures ​components for plastic explosives and ⁠the polymer used ​to produce ​solid ​propellant for ​Russian ‌ballistic missiles,” ​the ​defence ministry said on Telegram. Russia’s foreign ministry has accused ⁠Latvia of creating artificial ⁠obstacles ⁠to hinder the ​transit of Russian grain to ⁠global markets , saying the restrictions pose additional risks ⁠to global food security. Ministry ​spokesperson ‌Maria Zakharova ‌claimed in a statement published ‌on the ministry’s website on Friday that Latvia was conducting inspections of Russian grain shipments for allegedly ‌stolen Ukrainian agricultural products and was seeking ways ​to ban Russian grain transit altogether. stories.title: ‘Genuinely emotional’: the world-conquering Chicken Shop Date’s final, eye-opening episode
stories.summary: After a 12-year run, Amelia Dimoldenberg’s last episode of Chicken Shop Date – a therapy session with Esther Perel – is being shown in cinemas. It’s a fittingly grand finale for a YouTube cult favourite that far outgrew its medium The decision to screen the full final series of Chicken Shop Date in cinemas before the finale airs on YouTube is, it could be argued, overkill. The cinema is a place where you sit rapt among like-minded people, bombarded with cutting-edge sound design and world-class visuals. On the other hand, the fun interview show that is Chicken Shop Date is the thing I watch alone on my computer while I pick my toenails. It isn’t a natural fit, is what I’m trying to say. And yet, goddamn it if the whole thing didn’t leave me slightly choked up. After 12 years of flirting and awkwardness, Amelia Dimoldenberg’s final guest is Esther Perel, the Belgian psychotherapist and relationship guru beloved by Oprah Winfrey. It is by no means a traditional episode, almost completely dismissing the tone of everything that came before it. Dimoldenberg’s well-honed persona, alternately dismissive and needy, is nowhere to be seen. Instead, Dimoldenberg does something that Perel must be deadeningly familiar with when meeting new people: she uses the episode as a free therapy session. Continue reading...

Tiny Hat: a new Linux distro dedicated to retro gamedev
stories.summary: Tiny Hat uses only around 100MB of RAM after booting, and can be booted from a >= 1GB memory stick. It comes with a few small games, an easy way to install and run more games and several example programs for getting into retro game development. It also uses a modern stack of libraries, with dwl / Wayland, SDL3 and GTK4. One possible use is to buy a cheap x86 machine for younger members of a family, to completely brain wash inspire them into getting into graphics programming and appreciating retro games, perhaps as a Christmas present. At least a few people have found it fun so far, so I wanted to share it. Comments

stories.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
stories.summary: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. Update : Hah! Turns out I wrote about this application of sqlite_rsync back in October 2024 when the tool was first released. Tags: backups , sqlite
